note: Draft vectors for LIP-0022. No vector reads a node or a clock: tips, times, heights and the state of nodes are stated. Block hashes are placeholders. A vector whose outcome is not the passing one holds one defect and names a neighbour with the passing outcome that differs from it in that defect; a vector marked compound states several findings and names none, and a sequence states the outcome of each of its steps. No verdict of this file records a closure. S, LAG and K are the proposed values of three provisional numbers; a change of one of them changes the vectors at its boundary.

fields.observations: readings: the tips of the first and of the last read, the hash that the node gives for height 0, and where stated the tip read before the effect. facts: a block that holds a fact, and what the node gives for heights of its active chain.
fields.nodes: active_chain of the reading node maps a height to the hash that the node gives for it. headers_above_tip is how many blocks the best header that a node knows lies above its tip.
fields.clock: now, kept_mark, tip_header_time and first_sight are seconds of UTC. first_sight is absent where the verifier holds none for the tip, and the observation then writes it. class is absent where the action profile states none. now_before_effect is the second reading of B1.6.
fields.sequences: One verifier over time. start and end state what it keeps durably: the kept mark of B3.2 and the first sights of B3.7, a map from the hash of a block to a time. Each step is an observation with its reading of the clock, its tip and the expected outcome, or a restart, which changes nothing that is kept. finding states a refusal of section 1 or 2 that holds for that observation. control names a sequence without the defect.
fields.recent: blocks: committed_block_height is absent where the node does not know the committed hash. windows: the rule of LIP-0008 section 7.1 with a verdict and no code.
fields.depth: evidence.block_height is absent for a pending transaction.
fields.order: findings lists the codes that hold for one observation, in no particular order; expect is the one that B6.1 reports.

rules.title: an observation between two reads of the tip
a void observation proves nothing and closes nothing
rules.not_covered: No vector holds a closure. The vectors of B1.1 state the void observation.

rules.title: the pinned chain
a confirmed fact belongs to the observation
every fact of a check from one observation
rules.not_covered: The window vectors take the height of the tip from one observation. No vector holds a whole admission check, and none shows a fact from an earlier observation.

rules.title: the tip and the clock again before an effect
the reading node and the configured comparison nodes
rules.not_covered: node-07 states a verifier without a comparison node. No vector shows that a fact was taken from one, and none shows a configuration.

rules.title: when two nodes count as two
a healthy node
a tip agrees, is behind or conflicts
a healthy observation
the verifier's clock
rules.not_covered: No vector reads a clock; each states a reading.

rules.title: a clock that went back
a header ahead of the clock
the age of the tip: the larger of the header age and the seen age
the class of an action
the two cutoffs
the first sight of a tip
a first sight is written once and kept
rules.not_covered: The sequences state a restart as a step. No vector holds a store that was lost or that went back.

rules.title: the issuer commits the tip of its observation
rules.not_covered: No vector holds an issuer's observation.

rules.title: the recent block on the active chain
the anchor above the recent block
after a reorganisation
the depth of a confirmed fact
the larger of the signed minimum and the operator's floor
no comparison across chains
the order of the first six codes
the place of the other three
rules.not_covered: No vector holds a rule of a grant beside a refusal of this profile.

sequences.claim: The header of a tip is two hours ahead of the clock when the verifier first sees it, and no block follows. The first observation writes the first sight although B3.3 refuses it. When the clock has come within S of the header the seen age is 6600 seconds, and the tip is admitted for no action. A checker that measures the header age alone admits at the third and the fourth step.
A tip whose header is 20 seconds behind the clock at its first sight, and no block follows. Both classes are admitted until the header age reaches their cutoff.
The header of a tip is 600 seconds ahead of the clock at its first sight, which the proposed S allows. The action stops 3600 seconds after the first sight, when the header age is 3000 seconds.
The verifier restarts between two observations of one tip. The first sight is kept, and the seen age counts from it.
A new block arrives after the tip grew too old: the new tip has a first sight of its own, and the action is admitted again.
The tip goes to another block and comes back. The block that is the tip again has the first sight that it had. A checker that writes a first sight anew admits at the last step.
The clock reads one second less than a reading that the verifier has used, and reads more again afterwards. The kept mark stays through the refusal.
A block is the tip for the first time in an observation whose clock reads less than the kept mark. That observation writes no first sight; the next one does.
The first observation of a tip is refused because a comparison node conflicts. It writes the first sight all the same, and the seen age counts from it.
The first observation of a tip is void. It writes no first sight, and the seen age counts from the next observation.
